newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MADRID VICTORY GIVES DORTMUND EXTRA BOOST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MADRID VICTORY GIVES DORTMUND EXTRA BOOST.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's surprise 1-0 victory at Atletico Madrid in the champions' league on Wednesday has given the injury-hit German club a huge shot-in-the-arm before Sunday's crunch Bundesliga clash with Bayern Munich.

"A team that wins in Madrid can also win in Munich with the same kind of performance," captain Michael Zorc said on Thursday after Stefan Reuter celebrated his 30th birthday with one of the most important goals of his career in the Spanish capital.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld added: "It's sensational. You can't speak highly enough of this win."
The victory effectively secured the 1995 and 1996 Bundesliga champions a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup with three wins in as many games in Group B.
It provided a huge lift to Hitzfeld's team after they have struggled to be consistent in the German first division following an array of injuries to key players.
After 10 games, Dortmund are fourth in the table, four points behind record champions Bayern who moved level on points with leaders VfB Stuttgart last weekend.
A victory on Sunday evening in Munich's Olympic stadium would put Dortmund back on course on the domestic scene and help quash rumours that the club is suffering with internal squabbling.
"People on the outside have tried to create problems within the team," veteran German international defender Juergen Kohler said.
"Let's get it clear. There are no arguments and no cliques, otherwise a performance like this would not have been possible. Every player was ready to do each other's dirty work on the pitch."

Dortmund will again be without their key libero Matthias Sammer against Bayern but there were reports in Dortmund on Thursday that playmaker Andy Moeller may be fit enough to return after a pulled leg muscle.

Defender Markus Babbel and midfielder Markus Muench were both confined to bed on Wednesday because of illness. The Bavarians will also be without international wing-back Christian Ziege and defender Thomas Helmer because of injury.
Manager Uli Hoeness is refusing to let anybody start complaining about injury and illness problems, however, as the Bavarians prepare to defend their unbeaten run at home this season.
"We are always saying that we have 18 players of equal quality," Hoeness said. "As long as we have 12 fit players there is no reason to complain."
